hints: Every heartbeat has to start in the same place, look for X, the wave spreading from the sinoatrial node, and check what must happen immediately after in the atria.
Remember why the AV node exists, the impulse must arrive at V and then be held up at U before it is allowed to rush down to the ventricles via W.
walkthrough:
**Start at the pacemaker**

Think like the heart. It always starts at the sinoatrial node. That is X, wave of excitation spreads from the sinoatrial node.

What does that wave do first? It spreads across the atria, so the atrial walls contract. That is T. So we must have X followed by T.

**Get to the AV node and use the delay**

After the atria contract, the excitation reaches the atrioventricular node. That is V.

Then it is deliberately delayed a fraction of a second. That is U. This delay is vital, it lets the atria finish emptying blood into the ventricles before the ventricles contract.

**Fire the ventricles and loop round**

After the delay, the wave passes rapidly down the Purkyne tissue. That is W.

This causes the ventricles to contract. That is Y. Then the cycle resets back to X.

Full logical order is:
$$X \rightarrow T \rightarrow V \rightarrow U \rightarrow W \rightarrow Y \rightarrow X$$

**Match to the circular diagram**

The diagrams are circles, so you can start reading anywhere as long as the order round the circle is correct. Only C goes round in the order X, T, V, U, W, Y.

options.A: Starts with V then W then U, which puts Purkyne conduction before the AV node delay. The delay at U must come before W.
options.B: Puts U before V and Y before W, which is backwards. The wave must enter the AV node (V) before it can be delayed (U), and Purkyne conduction (W) must come before ventricular contraction (Y).
options.C: Shows the correct loop: X to T (atria contract), to V to U (AV node delay), to W to Y (ventricles contract). This allows atrial systole to complete before ventricular systole.
options.D: Swaps T and V, showing the wave entering the AV node before the atria contract. Atrial contraction (T) must follow the SAN wave (X) before the signal reaches the AV node.
